uncertainty_budget.explanation: The Indian market price of the token against the official rupee rate for a dollar. This is the bulk of the gap and it is the part everyone argues about.
No rate was published on the settlement date. Stepping back to 2026-06-25 or forward to 2026-06-29 is undetermined — Rule 206 does not say which.
A daily candle is not a price. It is a range with four printed readings and no rule choosing between them.
The retrieved pair is USDT/INR. The receipt was USDC. The figure is USDT/INR x USDC/USDT, and treating the peg as exactly 1.0000 is a further choice.

regimes.outcome: The receipt of 5,000 USDC is classified as income from the transfer of a virtual digital asset under s.115BBH, recognized on the date of receipt (2026-06-28), valued using the telegraphic transfer buying rate on the last day of the tax year (2026-03-31), and subject to TDS at 1% under s.393(1). If the assessee discloses all material facts and offers a bona fide explanation, no penalty will be imposed under s.439(8).
regimes.reasoning:
Classification: The receipt of 5,000 USDC is considered a virtual digital asset under s.2(47A). Since it is received and not transferred, it falls under the income from the transfer of a virtual digital asset under s.115BBH.

Recognition Date: According to Rule 56, the valuation date for income from the transfer of a virtual digital asset is the date of receipt, which is 2026-06-28.

Valuation Method: Rule 206 specifies that the value of income in foreign currency should be determined using the telegraphic transfer buying rate on the last day of the tax year (2026-03-31).

TDS: Under s.393(1), any sum by way of consideration for the transfer of a virtual digital asset is subject to TDS at 1%.

Penalty Position: Under s.439(8), if the assessee discloses all material facts and offers a bona fide explanation, no penalty will be imposed.
